holidays.name: National Static Electricity Day
holidays.description: A shocking day dedicated to the zaps, clingy socks, and hair-raising wonders of static electricity. Celebrate by rubbing a balloon on your head and sticking it to the wall.
holidays.origin: Static electricity has been studied since ancient Greece, when Thales of Miletus rubbed amber with fur and noticed it attracted light objects. The day is an unofficial observance, popular in science circles and winter-weary households when dry air makes shocks most common.
holidays.funFact: The word 'electricity' comes from the Greek word 'elektron,' meaning amber, because amber was the first material observed to hold a static charge.

holidays.name: National Apricot Day
holidays.description: A sweet-tart salute to the fuzzy orange fruit that is often overshadowed by peaches. Enjoy apricots fresh, dried, baked into pastries, or turned into jam.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance celebrating the apricot, a fruit cultivated for thousands of years in Central Asia and China before spreading along trade routes to Persia, Armenia, and the Mediterranean.
holidays.funFact: The apricot's scientific name, Prunus armeniaca, reflects the long-held belief that it originated in Armenia, though it likely first grew in Central Asia or China.

holidays.name: Play God Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day for exercising your power to make small, benevolent decisions that improve the lives of others, like paying for someone's coffee or picking the movie for movie night.
holidays.origin: Play God Day is a quirky unofficial observance that appears on lists of offbeat holidays. It is meant as a lighthearted invitation to use your influence for good rather than for smiting.
holidays.funFact: Many quirky holiday calendars mark it as a day to be generous and kind, so the most 'godlike' thing you can do is surprise a stranger with a good deed.

holidays.name: National Law Enforcement Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A day to thank police officers and other law enforcement personnel for their service, often with cards, baked goods, and the occasional box of donuts.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States since 2015, when a coalition of national police organizations and supporters backed a day of public gratitude for officers. It takes place every January 9.
holidays.funFact: The popular stereotype of cops and donuts partly traces back to the 1950s, when donut shops were among the few businesses open late at night and became natural gathering spots for patrol officers.

holidays.name: Cut Your Energy Costs Day
holidays.description: A practical but oddly cheerful day for hunting down drafty windows, unplugging idle gadgets, and bullying your thermostat into submission.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance placed in the heart of winter, when heating bills tend to arrive like unwelcome guests after the holiday spending spree.
holidays.funFact: Electronics left plugged in can keep drawing power even when switched off, a phenomenon nicknamed 'vampire power' or 'phantom load.'
